profileAndAuthorshipLimits.nativeRoute: actor_process.ts:1043 constructs the specialized native worker transport with claude. A declared codex profile is not proof that this native route selects or runs it.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.sameFamily: validator/qualification.ts:521-527 and 553-562 treat same declared family as ineligible; differing family permits remaining conditions only. Renaming primary/peer actors does not alter the relation.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.nativeClaudeAuthorship: For a scope genuinely authored by Claude through this route, another Claude assessment is ineligible even for author_distinct.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.mixedSurvivingAuthorship: For a scope whose established surviving authors include both declared families, neither of the two declared profiles is distinct from all authors. This is conditional on exact surviving scope attribution, not a broad history union.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.externalAttribution: Current dispatch at validator/qualification.ts:551 is unknown(external_attribution_requires_future_judgment) for external construction. The HOW explicitly says a prior acknowledged owner ruling is not joined there; an existing acknowledgment therefore does not resolve current pre-paid author missingness by itself.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.peerFamilyCardinalityInference: With at least one established author family and two required mutually independent peer assessments, each assessor must differ from the author and from the other assessor. The closed two-family policy cannot satisfy that combination even if bootstrap identity facts were supplied. This is a consequence of the present relation, not authority to add profiles or change policy.
profileAndAuthorshipLimits.independentResidual: These genuine production eligibility limits remain separate from the optional peer-bootstrap topology and from the bounded Q1/Q4 fail-closed repair.
